summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, and a history of multiple dialysis-related infections was admitted from rehab for fever and chills during dialysis. She had been experiencing persistent right flank pain and was found to have green pus in her urine, indicating acute bacterial cystitis. Blood and catheter tip cultures confirmed methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia, prompting removal of her infected dialysis line. An MRI revealed osteomyelitis at the T9 vertebra, necessitating a six-week course of intravenous vancomycin. She completed treatment for E. coli urinary infection with ceftriaxone and underwent a 'line holiday' before placement of a new tunneled dialysis catheter. Her blood pressure stabilized with infection treatment, and her leg ulcers showed improvement. She was discharged to extended care to complete antibiotic therapy with close monitoring.
